A resonant mode stores energy in fields and circuit elements. Energy
participation asks where that energy is concentrated. It connects a mode's
field distribution to particular dielectrics, interfaces and junctions, helping
you interpret which modeled channels could contribute to loss.

The [energy-participation method of Minev et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.00620)
uses modes of a linearized Josephson circuit as inputs to quantization.
SCGSim provides the supported electromagnetic participation and loss quantities;
a participation plot alone does not supply a nonlinear Hamiltonian, Kerr
coefficients or a qubit lifetime.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  F["Mode fields"] --> P["Energy partitions"]
  P --> V["Bulk / surface / junction"]
  V --> L["Known-loss contributions"]
  A["Material loss assumptions"] --> L
```

## Three views of a mode {#workflow-and-state-contract}

| View | Energy attributed to | Physical question |
|---|---|---|
| Bulk | A modeled dielectric volume | How much electric energy lies in this material? |
| Surface | A thin-film interface estimate | How strongly does the field sample this interface? |
| Junction/port | A declared linearized circuit element | How does this element participate in the mode? |

A surface estimate uses the field at an interface to estimate energy in a film
with specified thickness and permittivity. Metal-air, metal-substrate and
substrate-air describe different interfaces and field components. Bulk and
surface views are not automatically disjoint pieces of a complete energy budget.
The junction model supplies its inductance and any declared capacitance; it
represents the linearized element used in the electromagnetic calculation.

## Quantities and normalization {#quantities-and-normalization}

For an energy numerator $U_i$, participation is dimensionless:

$$
p_i = \frac{U_i}{U_{\mathrm{norm}}}.
$$

Read the numerator and denominator together. AEDT uses the electric energy of
unique physical domains plus declared junction capacitive energy. Palace uses
its final native electric-domain and capacitive-energy tables. Thin-film energy
estimates are numerators and are not added back into these denominators.
The [surface and junction formulas](specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#surface-estimates-and-junction-normalization)
define the field convention and each supported quantity.

The backends also differ physically. Palace reports signed native port
participation, which depends on the mode's phase convention. AEDT's inductive
$p_L$ and capacitive $p_C$ are nonnegative energy ratios. These quantities need
their own interpretation rather than direct comparison as interchangeable
junction numbers.

State the exterior boundary and vacuum-region size alongside the geometry.
Palace's unspecified Eigenmode exterior uses natural PMC. The documented AEDT
EPR policy uses HFSS's default Perfect E on background-exposed surfaces of its
native Region. A particular study's prepared native model determines its actual
boundary; a layout preview alone does not establish it. A shared layout does
not equalize these field models.

## Interfaces and loss assumptions {#surface-identity-masks-and-loss-assumptions}

For a dielectric channel with a known loss tangent, the modeled contribution is

$$
Q_i^{-1} = p_i\tan\delta_i.
$$

Both factors matter: a strongly sampled low-loss material and a weakly sampled
high-loss film can have different effects. Film thickness, permittivity and
loss tangent are model assumptions, not quantities determined by the layout.
A known-loss sum covers only evaluated channels with specified losses. It is
not total device $Q$ or $T_1$, and does not account for omitted mechanisms.

An explicit zero loss tangent is a known zero contribution. An unspecified loss
tangent is unknown, so its inverse-$Q$ contribution is unavailable even when
participation is known. Likewise, uncomputed energy is not zero energy.

::: {.callout-note title="Reading older Palace results" collapse="true"}
For Palace surface-film records preceding v2, a recorded zero loss tangent has
ambiguous origin. The reader preserves the raw value but treats its effective
loss as unknown; the inverse-$Q$ contribution remains unavailable.
:::

Mask margins provide alternative interface estimates. Read the unmasked
baseline and each requested margin separately, including a requested zero
margin; do not add them as disjoint bands. AEDT evaluates horizontal top/bottom
interfaces and does not calculate sidewall film energy. Palace sidewalls also
remain uncomputed where they were not selected. Changing a film-loss assumption
on stored evidence can revise the loss estimate without another field solve;
it does not recompute the field or alter the modeled geometry.

Native solver $Q$ and this model-derived loss budget answer different questions.
Native $Q$ reflects the mechanisms represented in that solver calculation;
$p\tan\delta$ attributes loss to the selected material model. Palace can report
native infinite $Q$ without establishing a physically lossless device. Keep
that observation separate from unknown losses and the finite-Q view described
in the [native Q reference](specs/palace-eigenmode.qmd#native-eigenmode-q).

## Explore a result

Start with the [resonance/EPR tutorial](tutorials/resonance-epr.qmd), then use
[offline EPR](course/offline-epr.qmd) to inspect recorded modes and revise loss
assumptions. The [examples](examples.qmd) connect the physical model to its
backend workflow.

For binding and API details, use the [AEDT EPR reference](specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#public-epr-candidate-surface)
and [Palace Eigenmode reference](specs/palace-eigenmode.qmd). The
[report reference](report-model.qmd#eigenmode-epr-presentation) describes
selections, ordering and the separation of baseline, margin and unavailable
quantities.
